newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian sugar prices bounce back after losses.
newsitem.headline: Indian sugar prices bounce back after losses.

text.p: Indian sugar prices on Friday bounced back after recent losses on the local market, dealers said.
Consumer buying remained slow but thin arrivals and a shortage of ready stock dragged prices up.

"Earlier in the week local millers were witnessing low demand from central India due to a traders strike but this strike was called off yesterday and local millers are again witnessing higher outstation buying," one broker said.
"Higher outstation buying at the mill level had curtailed arrivals of sugar from mills to the market," he added.

In the ready delivery sugar S-30 rose by five rupees at 1,415/1,435 rupees per quintal while M-30 rose by the same margin at 1,445/1,485 rupees. Sugar mill delivery moved up to 1,350/1,365 rupees per quintal from 1,340/1,360 rupees.
